options: A one-dimensional column of values where each value has an index label
A two-dimensional table with rows and columns
A Python list that cannot be changed
A SQL query stored in a variable
questions.explain: A Series is a labeled one-dimensional array: values plus an index, and optionally a name.

questions.q: What do you get back from customers["city"] when customers is a DataFrame?
questions.explain: Selecting one column with square brackets returns a Series. A DataFrame is a collection of Series sharing an index.

questions.q: Which is the most readable way to build a small DataFrame by hand?
options: A list of column names followed by a separate list of index labels
A dictionary where each key is a column name and each value is a list for that column
A single string containing the whole table
questions.explain: pd.DataFrame({...}) with column names as keys and lists as values is the standard hand-built form.

questions.q: A DataFrame has 5 rows and 4 columns. What does df.shape return?
questions.explain: shape is a tuple of (rows, columns). It is an attribute, so it is written without parentheses.

questions.q: A DataFrame is created with no index argument. What index does pandas give it?
options: No index at all, so rows cannot be referenced
A default RangeIndex counting up from 0
questions.explain: Without an explicit index, pandas creates a RangeIndex starting at 0.
